html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; RDS: Relational Database Service

  • Define cloud computing and tell the service models apart
  • Name the six advantages of the AWS Cloud and match each to a situation
  • Explain speed, global reach, high availability and elasticity
  • Compare fixed and variable cost and the costs of running your own data center
  • Describe licensing options, rightsizing and automation as ways to control cost

2The value of the cloud

Running case

Tidewater Weighs Its Server Room

  • Tidewater Outfitters rents a small server room that runs its online shop
  • Sales triple at the holidays and then fall, yet the servers are sized for the peak all year
  • Buying more hardware takes weeks, and new customers in Europe see slow pages
  • The finance lead owns Windows Server licenses and wants to keep using them
  • Your job: explain what moving to AWS would change, in benefits and in cost

What Is Cloud Computing?

  • Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet, with pay-as-you-go pricing
  • Instead of owning servers and data centers, you use computing, storage and databases from a provider such as AWS
  • You pay for what you use, and you can stop when you no longer need a resource
  • The provider takes care of the facilities, hardware and power; you choose and use the services
Exam tip

"On demand" plus "pay as you go" is the core definition of cloud computing.

Service Models: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS Beyond the guide

  • Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): the basic building blocks (networking, compute and storage) with the most control for you
  • Platform as a Service (PaaS): removes the need to manage the underlying infrastructure, so you focus on your application
  • Software as a Service (SaaS): a complete product that the provider runs and manages, such as web-based email
  • Going from IaaS to SaaS, you manage less and the provider manages more

Exam tip

More control means more to manage: IaaS gives the most control, SaaS the least.

The Value Proposition: Six Advantages

  • Trade fixed expense for variable expense: pay only when you consume
  • Massive economies of scale: a lower variable cost than on your own
  • Stop guessing capacity: scale up and down as required
  • Increase speed and agility: resources in minutes, not weeks
  • Stop running and maintaining data centers: focus on your business
  • Go global in minutes: deploy in several Regions with a few clicks

Exam tip

Know all six; questions often describe one of them in different words.

Speed of Deployment and Agility

  • In the cloud, new IT resources are a click away, so the wait for developers falls from weeks to minutes
  • Experimenting costs less money and less time, which makes the organization more agile
  • Teams can try different instance types, storage or setups quickly and drop what does not work
  • Tidewater tip: a new test environment for the holiday sale is ready the same day, not after a hardware order
Exam tip

Speed of deployment means minutes instead of weeks; agility means the cost of trying things is low.

Global Reach in Minutes

  • With the AWS global infrastructure you can deploy an application in several AWS Regions around the world with a few clicks
  • Customers connect to resources close to them, which gives lower latency and a better experience
  • It costs little extra to reach new markets, because you do not build new data centers
  • Tidewater tip: a second Region near Europe makes the shop faster for European customers
  • Regions and Availability Zones are covered in Module 6
Exam tip

Global reach is about deploying close to customers; lower latency is the benefit to remember.

High Availability

  • High availability means a workload keeps running when part of it fails
  • Use several smaller resources and spread requests across them, so they do not share one point of failure
  • AWS design guidance: monitor, recover automatically and test your recovery
  • AWS builds its infrastructure from Regions and Availability Zones, so you can spread a workload across locations

Exam tip

For "keeps working after a failure", think high availability and no single point of failure.

Elasticity: Capacity That Follows Demand

  • Elasticity means adding and removing resources as demand changes
  • On premises you buy for the peak, and the extra capacity sits idle the rest of the time
  • In the cloud you stop guessing capacity: scale up and down with a few minutes' notice
  • Both risks go away: expensive idle resources and too little capacity
  • Auto scaling is the AWS feature behind it (Module 7)

Exam tip

Elasticity works in both directions: it adds capacity when demand rises and removes it when demand falls.

Which Benefit Is It?

Situation Benefit
A test environment ready in minutes, not weeks Speed and agility
Extra servers for the holiday sale, removed after Elasticity
European customers served from a nearby Region Global reach
The shop stays up when one location fails High availability
Paying per use instead of buying servers first Fixed to variable expense
Lower prices because many customers share the cost Economies of scale
Exam tip

Find the key phrase: "minutes" means speed, "both directions" means elasticity, "close to customers" means global reach.

Fixed Costs and Variable Costs

  • Fixed expense: you invest in data centers and servers before you know how you will use them
  • Variable expense: you pay only when you consume resources, and only for how much you consume
  • Adopt a consumption model: a development environment used 8 hours a day on weekdays can be stopped when idle, which AWS puts at about 75% savings (40 hours against 168)
  • Variable cost lowers the risk of buying too much or too little

Exam tip

"Trade fixed expense for variable expense" means pay for what you use instead of buying capacity first.

Costs of Running Your Own Data Center

  • Running your own means procurement (buying and waiting), maintenance and capacity planning
  • It also means the heavy lifting: racking, stacking and powering servers, and managing operating systems and applications
  • AWS does the data center work, and managed services remove much of the operating burden
  • That effort moves from running infrastructure to using services and serving customers
  • You still pay for the services you use, and for the people who design and run your workloads
Exam tip

On-premises costs are more than hardware: add buying, upkeep, power, space and staff time.

Economies of Scale

  • Usage from hundreds of thousands of customers is aggregated in the cloud
  • That lets AWS achieve higher economies of scale, which become lower pay-as-you-go prices
  • You can reach a lower variable cost than you could on your own
  • Tidewater tip: a small shop gets prices built on the volume of a very large provider
  • Prices still differ by Region and service, and are covered in Module 13
Exam tip

Economies of scale: many customers share the cost, so each pays less per unit.

Licensing: Bring Your Own License or License Included

  • Bring Your Own License (BYOL): reuse licenses you already own on AWS, which can save cost
  • Included license: the license cost is part of the price of the AWS resource
  • BYOL needs you to follow the vendor's license terms and track usage; an included license is simpler
  • License Manager can switch a workload between the two license types without redeploying it

Exam tip

BYOL means you bring a license you own; included means the license is already in the price.

3Cloud economics and practice

AWS License Manager

  • AWS License Manager manages software licenses from vendors such as Microsoft, SAP, Oracle and IBM
  • It works across Regions and accounts and gives dashboards for usage and vendor audits
  • Rule-based limits, hard or soft, stop non-compliant use before it happens
  • It tracks software licensed by vCPUs, physical cores, sockets or machines
  • It integrates with Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, AWS Marketplace, Systems Manager and AWS Organizations
Exam tip

Tracking licenses and staying compliant on AWS: AWS License Manager.

Rightsizing: Matching Size to Workload

  • Rightsizing is matching instance types and sizes to your workload
  • AWS calls it the most effective way to control cloud costs
  • Migrated workloads are often oversized, because speed came before cost
  • Review usage continuously, shut down idle resources and resize overprovisioned ones
  • Needs change, so treat rightsizing as ongoing, not a one-time task

Exam tip

Too big wastes money and too small hurts performance; rightsizing finds the match.

Tools That Help: Compute Optimizer and Cost Explorer

  • AWS Compute Optimizer gives recommendations that show where an instance can be resized
  • AWS Cost Explorer helps you analyze costs and usage over time
  • Tags let you assign cost to teams and workloads, so waste has an owner
  • AWS suggests a rightsizing schedule for each team and tagging every instance
  • Pricing and billing tools are covered in Module 13
Exam tip

Resize recommendations: Compute Optimizer. Looking at past spend: Cost Explorer.

Automation: Faster, Repeatable, Less Error-Prone

  • AWS design guidance: perform operations as code, so procedures are versioned, tested and automated
  • Manage change through automation, and recover from failure automatically
  • Automation can add or remove resources to match demand, which supports elasticity
  • Fewer manual steps mean faster, more repeatable work and fewer mistakes
  • Experimenting with different configurations becomes cheap when resources are automatable
Exam tip

Benefits of automation: speed, consistency and less manual effort.

What the Exam Asks: Value and Economics

  • Elasticity or high availability: capacity follows demand, or the workload survives failure
  • Agility or global reach: speed of change, or closeness to customers
  • Fixed or variable expense: pay first, or pay as you use
  • BYOL or included license: a license you own, or one in the price
  • Compute Optimizer or Cost Explorer: resize advice, or spend analysis
  • IaaS, PaaS or SaaS: how much you manage
Exam tip

Name the situation first, then the benefit.

Design Check: Tidewater's Move

Tidewater's situation The cloud idea
Holiday spikes, idle the rest of the year Elasticity: scale up and down, pay for use
Buying servers before knowing demand Fixed to variable expense
New customers in Europe and Asia Global reach: deploy in more Regions
Windows Server licenses already owned BYOL, tracked with License Manager
Servers oversized after the move Rightsizing with Compute Optimizer
Release steps repeated by hand Automation: operations as code
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

Common Traps: Value and Economics

  • Elasticity is not high availability: one changes capacity with demand, the other survives failure
  • Variable expense is not always cheaper: pay-per-use rewards stopping and rightsizing resources
  • Agility is about speed of change, not uptime
  • BYOL is not automatic: it depends on the vendor's license terms
  • More control means more to manage: IaaS gives the most control and the most work
Exam tip

If two answers both sound good, check which one matches the exact benefit in the question.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which statement best describes cloud computing?

  • ABuying and owning servers in a rented room so that capacity is always available
  • BSigning a multi-year contract for a fixed amount of computing power
  • COn-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
  • DRunning every application only on a private network inside the company
Show the answer

Answer: C. Cloud computing delivers resources on demand over the internet and charges for what you use. Owning servers, a fixed multi-year contract and a purely private network describe traditional approaches rather than cloud computing.

S2A team can launch a new test environment in minutes instead of waiting weeks for hardware. Which cloud benefit does this describe?

  • AIncreased speed and agility
  • BMassive economies of scale
  • CGlobal reach in minutes
  • DA guarantee of high availability
Show the answer

Answer: A. Getting resources in minutes instead of weeks is the speed-of-deployment side of agility. Economies of scale are about lower prices, global reach is about deploying near customers, and high availability is about surviving failures.

S3Tidewater's traffic triples at the holidays and then falls. Which cloud benefit lets the shop add capacity for the season and release it afterwards?

  • AGlobal reach
  • BEconomies of scale
  • CHigh availability
  • DElasticity
Show the answer

Answer: D. Elasticity means adding and removing resources as demand changes, so the shop pays for the extra capacity only while it needs it. Global reach, economies of scale and high availability do not describe capacity that follows demand.

S4Which TWO are advantages of cloud computing? (Select TWO.)

  • ATrade fixed expense for variable expense
  • BEvery workload always costs less than it did on premises
  • CIncrease speed and agility
  • DAWS takes over all responsibility for your application's security
  • ECapacity planning is no longer needed in any form
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Paying as you use and gaining speed and agility are two of the six advantages. The cloud does not guarantee lower cost for every workload, does not remove your own security duties, and does not remove the need to think about capacity.

S5Which description best fits high availability?

  • AA workload that automatically gets larger every night
  • BA workload that keeps running when part of it fails
  • CA workload that costs the least possible amount per hour
  • DA workload that is stored in the Region nearest to its owner
Show the answer

Answer: B. High availability is about continuing to run despite failures, usually by spreading work across several resources with no single point of failure. Growing automatically is elasticity, lowest cost is cost optimization, and nearest Region is about latency.

S6Which statement describes a variable expense?

  • AYou pay only for the resources you consume, in the amount you consume
  • BYou pay a large amount up front before you know how you will use the resources
  • CYou pay the same amount every month whether or not you use the resources
  • DYou pay once for equipment that you then own for many years
Show the answer

Answer: A. Variable expense follows consumption: you pay when you use resources and only for what you use. Paying up front, paying a flat amount regardless of use, and buying equipment outright are fixed expenses.

S7Tidewater already owns Windows Server licenses and wants to reuse them on AWS to save cost. Which approach fits?

  • ALicense-included instances, which add the license cost to the hourly price
  • BBring Your Own License (BYOL), reusing licenses it already owns
  • CPay-as-you-go licenses from a reseller that sits outside AWS
  • DA new data center purchased just to hold the licenses
Show the answer

Answer: B. BYOL lets a company reuse licenses it already owns, subject to the vendor's terms. License-included instances charge for a license it does not need, and the other options add cost or complexity without using the licenses it has.

S8After the move, Tidewater's servers run at about ten percent CPU use. Which practice reduces cost without losing the capacity the shop needs?

  • AMove to larger instance types so that there is more headroom
  • BAdd more instances so that the load is spread thinner
  • CRightsize by matching instance sizes to the workload
  • DTurn off all monitoring so that no one sees the low use
Show the answer

Answer: C. Rightsizing matches instance types and sizes to what the workload really uses, so idle capacity stops costing money. Larger or additional instances raise cost, and turning off monitoring removes the information needed to rightsize.

S9Which TWO AWS tools help you find and act on rightsizing and spending opportunities? (Select TWO.)

  • AAmazon Cognito
  • BAWS Compute Optimizer
  • CAWS Secrets Manager
  • DAWS Cost Explorer
  • EAWS Artifact
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Compute Optimizer recommends where instances can be resized, and Cost Explorer lets you analyze costs and usage. Cognito handles app sign-in, Secrets Manager stores secrets and Artifact provides compliance reports.

S10Which statement about economies of scale in the cloud is correct?

  • AEach customer's usage is priced on its own with no effect from other customers
  • BHigher usage across all customers makes prices rise for everyone
  • CEconomies of scale apply only to long-term storage services
  • DAggregated usage from many customers lets AWS offer lower pay-as-you-go prices
Show the answer

Answer: D. Because usage from a very large number of customers is combined, AWS achieves economies of scale and passes lower pay-as-you-go prices to customers. The other statements deny or reverse that effect.

S11Tidewater runs a development environment only during an eight-hour working day. Which action best applies the consumption model?

  • AStop the environment when it is not in use, so it runs only when needed
  • BKeep it running all day and night so that it starts instantly each morning
  • CBuy a larger instance so that tests finish faster and cost less overall
  • DCopy the environment to a second Region so that it is always on
Show the answer

Answer: A. The consumption model means paying only for what you use, so stopping idle resources cuts the bill. Running around the clock, buying larger instances or adding a second Region increases what you pay.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Cloud computing on-demand IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing; IaaS, PaaS and SaaS differ in what you manage
Six advantages variable expense, economies of scale, no capacity guessing, speed and agility, no data center upkeep, global reach
Resilience and demand high availability avoids single points of failure; elasticity adds and removes capacity
Cost model fixed expense is paid first, variable expense follows use; own data centers add buying, upkeep and staff
Licenses BYOL reuses what you own, an included license is in the price, License Manager tracks it
Cost control rightsize with Compute Optimizer, analyze with Cost Explorer, and automate
